note: Resolves exact authenticated dual-stack differences. Built-in defaults accept TEXT_ONLY/JAVA_UNHANDLED_500/JAVA_RAW_HTTP_4XX, fail RUST_FAILS_WHERE_JAVA_OK/RUST_OTHER_CODE, and leave the rest OPEN. Every explicit acceptance names endpoint + variant + category and documents its root cause; no category-wide defaults or endpoint-wide exemptions.
rule_predicates: allowed_paths are exact leaves by default; only subtree_paths opt into descendants. Every allowed path requires typed value/presence predicates. Complete data_diffs evidence records presence explicitly and [len] carries every unmatched row, checked against exhaustive declared row predicates. Missing evidence never matches.
known_limitations: Identity correspondence is checked bijectively within each journey and within each standalone response, not across journeys or sweep requests. UUID-shaped values participate at paired structural positions and captures; known integer PKs/references are scoped to device, deviceType, deviceDescription, deviceScoringRule, groupNetTrain and router-room domains. Explicitly masked fields and non-opted-in embedded JSON/entity-toString keys are outside that identity scope; clocks remain shape-normalized. Unobserved entities cannot establish intended reference semantics, and both stacks making the same mistake is not ruled out.

comparison_notes.endpoint:POST /api/radiotelephone/listPa: Deliberate difference (B7), not expressible in the harness (it always sends a JSON body, so a body-less POST cannot be replayed). curl on the dual stack: no Content-Type and no body -> Java HTTP 415, Rust 200 empty list (the frontend ditto/menu pages send exactly this because axios 0.26 drops Content-Type when data is absent; Rust keeps 200, Java 415 is an online defect). Content-Type: application/json with an empty body, and with body null -> both stacks HTTP 200 code 200 data []. Body {} -> both 200 code 202 (type required).
comparison_notes.journey:personal-telegram/floor-content: No DATA exemption. Java findByFloorIdIn has no ORDER BY; handleMaps appends query rows into ArrayList values of a HashMap. A live fixed-PK probe returns Java T(sort=1), E(sort=0) versus Rust E(sort=0), T(sort=1), so row order is unspecified, not identical ordered E/T. The opt-in floor_content comparison validates each stack's sole key and every row's floorId against its captured requested floor, substitutes only the object key, and compares all raw row identifiers/references through the journey bijection while matching complete field/value/Morse multisets. Changed or missing/extra rows and ambiguous identity matches fail normally.
comparison_notes.journey:b5-general-key-cable-two-student: Deliberate difference (B6), not copied: the electronic-key export (getTrainInfo/getTrainInfoBatch) carries pageDto[*].id. Java types that id as Integer while general_key_pat_page.id is a UUID string, so GeneralKeyPatPageSyncDto converts it to null (fixed cable) or to an unstable number (random report); Rust exports the real UUID, which importTrainInfo regenerates anyway. The journeys mask exactly $.data.pageDto[*].id because the unordered pageDto multiset is matched on whole rows and Java's garbage ids would misalign every other column; all other pageDto fields (key, pageNumber, sort, time, value, trainId) and the clock-derived trainDto.validTime remain compared. No override rule can express Java's mixed null/number ids per row.

Java answers 208 with description equal to the message; Rust leaves the description empty. The frontend never reads the response-level description.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. The Vue page creates a training without a duration, and the update path never sets one, so a paused training has duration NULL. Creating the next training of that type makes Java finish the paused one and call Integer.valueOf(duration) in TelexPatTrainStatisticalService.statistical, which throws NumberFormatException: Java answers 202 'Cannot parse null string', rolls the whole save back and leaves the user unable to start a new training until the paused one is finished. Rust counts a missing duration as 0 seconds and succeeds.
Follows from create-next: Java rolled back, so the paused predecessor stays status 2; Rust finished it (status 3).

Java defect deliberately not reproduced (IDOR). EnteringTelexPatService.save finds the record by id and type only, never by owner, and then overwrites the totals and sets createUserId to the caller: any user who knows or guesses another user's record id takes the record over. Rust answers 207 无权限 and leaves the record untouched. The Vue page only ever sends the id it received from findByUserIdAndType for its own record.
Follows from foreign-save: Java handed the record to the other user, so the owner's find returns the empty default; Rust kept it and returns the owner's record.
Follows from foreign-save: Java now shows the taken-over record to the intruder, Rust shows the empty default because nothing was written.

Both stacks refuse (HTTP 200, code 500, nothing written); only the text differs. Java leaks Hibernate's StaleObjectStateException message ('Row was updated or deleted by another transaction ... EnteringTelexPatEntity#<id>') from merging a detached entity with an unknown id; Rust says '训练记录不存在或类型不符'. The page ignores the save response.

Both stacks refuse (code 500, nothing written); Java leaks 'detached entity passed to persist' (an empty id slips past the duplicate check and breaks the persist), Rust reports the missing record. Text-only.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. findByIdAndType misses (type differs), so Java merges a detached entity that has the existing id and silently re-types the user's record without the one-record-per-type check; it adds/updates the new child-type statistics and leaves the former child-type statistics unchanged. Rust treats an id whose record has another type as 'not found' (code 500, nothing written). The page always sends the type it read the record with.

Follows from the registered retyping defect: Java changed the existing training record from type 6 to 7, so type 6 returns its empty default. Rust refused the retyping and still returns the unchanged type-6 record.
Follows from the registered retyping defect: Java now returns the retyped record for type 7. Rust refused the save without writing and returns the empty type-7 default.

Java defect deliberately not reproduced. A save without a type is not rejected by Java: it persists an orphan record with type NULL (and createUserId set) and a statistics row with child_type NULL. The Vue page always sends the type of the route it was opened with, and the Rust save answers 202 without writing.

Sweep artefact caused by the Java defect above: the preceding empty save left a statistics row with child_type NULL, and EnteringExerciseService.statisticalPage groups by childType (Collectors.groupingBy rejects the null key), so Java answers 500 for that user from then on. Rust never writes such rows and returns the four categories.
